subject: Vulnerability Playbook: SLA matrix, CVE routing and audit trace
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@auditfirm.com>, security@acmepay.com, thirdparty-scanner@secscan.io
Date: Mon, 10 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vulnerability Playbook: SLA matrix, CVE routing and audit trace

Team and partners —

Attaching a slimmed-down playbook for the SIG/SOC review: the SLA matrix (xls), a CVE routing flow diagram (png) and a recent scan snapshot (json). Auditor Sara asked for a single-page mapping that shows:
- who owns triage within 24h for critical/high
- where escalations to infra/eng happen
- where we keep audit traces for evidence requests

What I need today:
1) Kimberly — can you review the SLA table and confirm the ownership rows (we currently show: App Security = triage 24h, Infra Eng = remediation windows for infra components)
2) Rishi — can you confirm the CVE routing flow matches the integration with our Dedicated deployment teams (we need the path that shows fallbacks to regional capacity and the expected timelines for hotfix vs config mitigation)
3) Lauren — if Acme's auditor needs a signed attestation, can you prepare the short attestation language (one paragraph) we can append to the SIG packet?

Attachments: sla-matrix-v1.2.xlsx (sheet: SLA-by-severity), cve-routing-flowchart.png, scan-snapshot-20280608.json

Thanks — trying to close this before the auditor checkpoint at EOD PT.

—
Mina Haddad
Security Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@auditfirm.com>, security@acmepay.com
Date: Mon, 10 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vulnerability Playbook: SLA matrix, CVE routing and audit trace

Mina — quick pass from AppSec. I made three small edits to the SLA sheet and attached an updated workbook (sla-matrix-v1.3.xlsx). Summary of changes:
- Clarified that "Triage" is the initial vuln assessment (not full root-cause) and set expected triage completion to 24 hours for critical, 72 hours for high.
- Added a column for "Evidence Location" (Drive path) so auditors can find the traces quickly.
- Noted exception process for third-party dependencies (see row: 3rd-party-deps).

Rishi — on the routing diagram: I flagged two ambiguous arrows where infra team ownership could be interpreted as either "Regional infra" or "Platform SRE". If you confirm the right path, I'll update the PNG and the sheet.

Attachment: sla-matrix-v1.3.xlsx (updated)

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Director, App Security
Redwood Inference
From: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@auditfirm.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acmepay.com
Date: Mon, 10 Jun 2028 16:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vulnerability Playbook: SLA matrix, CVE routing and audit trace

Thanks for the packet — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying questions before the SIG submission:

1) Evidence retention: can you confirm how long you keep the raw scan snapshots referenced in the sheet? We need dates and the Drive locations.
2) SLA enforcement: do you have an internal metric or dashboard we can reference showing average triage time for the last 90 days for "critical" findings? A URL is fine if access is granted.
3) Signed attestation: the client (Acme) prefers the attestation to include a statement that Redwood will notify affected customers within 72 hours of an externally reported critical CVE that impacts a customer-managed deployment. Can you confirm or propose alternate wording?

If you can reply by EOD PT tomorrow, we can include your responses in the SIG packet.

Regards,
Sara Jensen
Senior Audit Manager
Northbridge Audit Partners
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@auditfirm.com>, security@acmepay.com
Date: Tue, 11 Jun 2028 14:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vulnerability Playbook: SLA matrix, CVE routing and audit trace

Closing the loop here with the operational confirmation and proposed attestation. Answers inline below —

On evidence retention: we retain raw scan snapshots (agent+authenticity metadata) for 365 days by default in the secure evidence bucket; critical snapshots are flagged and retained for 3 years. Drive links (read-only, auditor access): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-sla-playbook (already included in SLA sheet).

On SLA metric/dashboard: AppSec maintains a dashboard (internal Grafana) with a 90-day rolling average for triage times. We will provide temporary read-only viewer links to the auditor for the specific dashboard panels. (Jira: SEC-842 to track access).

On the 72-hour notification wording: suggested attestation paragraph below — feel free to paste into the SIG packet: 

"Redwood Inference confirms that for customer-managed deployments, Redwood will notify affected customers within 72 hours of receiving validated information that a public, customer-impacting critical CVE exists, subject to applicable confidentiality and legal constraints. Notifications will include a preliminary assessment and the planned mitigation or workaround. Where immediate mitigation is not feasible, Redwood will provide compensating controls and a remediation timeline."

Operational notes:
- Confirmed route: Regional Infra -> Platform SRE -> AppSec for hotfix coordination (updated flowchart attached: cve-routing-flowchart-v2.png).
- Exception handling: third-party dependency issues that require vendor coordination are documented in the sheet under "3rd-party-deps" and have SLA: vendor-engagement 7 days for engagement/triage.

Attachments referenced: cve-routing-flowchart-v2.png (updated), sla-matrix-v1.3.xlsx (as Kimberly updated), scan-snapshot-20280608.json

If everyone agrees, Mina can drop the attestation paragraph into the SIG packet and we can upload the final bundle to the Drive link for auditor delivery.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Platform Security
Redwood Inference
